newsitem.title: UK: Japan shipowners draw up new tanker safety measure.
newsitem.headline: Japan shipowners draw up new tanker safety measure.

text.p: The Japanese Shipowners' Association has mapped out safety measures for tankers navigating in Japan's congested waters, the Jiji Press agency reported on Wednesday.
The association said it will begin an immediate review of navigation conditions for large tankers entering Tokyo Bay and other congested waters round Japan.
The shipowners said they would also promote a switch to double-hulled tankers, which are less likely to cause oil spillages when the vessel runs aground.
The association will also ask the government to increase the number of large oilspill collection vessels. Japan currently has only one such vessel, the Seiryu Maru stationed in Ise Bay.

It wants spill collection vessels to be based in Tokyo Bay, the Inland Sea area, the Kyushu southern Japan area and in the Sea of Japan. The association said it would be prepared to shoulder an unspecified element of the costs involved.
The new safety measures were drawn up at the request of the Transport Ministry and the Maritime Safety Agency following the oil spill from the VLCC Diamond Grace earlier this month in Tokyo Bay.
